# Digital Health System for Philippine Community Health Nonprofit

## Recommended Approach: Hybrid Offline-First System

Given the constraints, I recommend a **locally-hosted, offline-capable system** rather than cloud-dependent solutions. This prioritizes resilience over connectivity.

---

## Specific Technology Stack

### Core System
**OpenMRS (Open Medical Records System)** - Free, open-source
- Offline-capable with local sync when connectivity returns
- Designed for low-resource settings
- Runs on modest hardware
- Large community support in developing countries

**Alternative (if OpenMRS too complex):** Medic Mobile's Community Health Toolkit - specifically built for offline field work

### Hardware
| Item | Specification | Cost (PHP) |
|------|---------------|-----------|
| Server (used Dell/HP) | i5, 8GB RAM, 500GB SSD | 25,000 |
| Backup server (identical) | For redundancy | 25,000 |
| 25 Android tablets | For field staff (offline-capable) | 150,000 |
| 4 desktop computers | Office/data entry | 60,000 |
| UPS systems (2x) | 2-3 hour backup power | 30,000 |
| Solar power system | 500W panel + battery | 40,000 |
| Network equipment | Router, switches, cables | 15,000 |
| **Hardware Subtotal** | | **345,000** |

### Software & Services
| Item | Cost (PHP) |
|------|-----------|
| OpenMRS setup & customization | 20,000 |
| Staff training (3 days, 30 people) | 15,000 |
| Documentation in Tagalog/local language | 8,000 |
| Contingency (10%) | 12,000 |
| **Software Subtotal** | **55,000** |

### **TOTAL: PHP 400,000** ✓

---

## Implementation Timeline (18 months)

**Months 1-2:** Hardware procurement, server setup, network installation
**Months 3-4:** OpenMRS configuration, data migration from paper (sample records)
**Months 5-6:** Staff training in cohorts (10 people/week)
**Months 7-12:** Phased rollout by department; parallel paper records
**Months 13-18:** Full transition; troubleshooting; documentation refinement

---

## What Happens After Donor Funding Ends (Month 18+)

### The Critical Problem
This is where most digitization projects fail in low-resource settings. Here's the honest assessment:

**Costs that will recur:**
- Server maintenance & replacement parts: ~PHP 20,000/year
- Electricity for servers: ~PHP 15,000/year
- Occasional staff retraining: ~PHP 8,000/year
- **Total annual operating cost: ~PHP 43,000/year**

### Sustainability Strategy (Built Into This Plan)

**1. Cost Absorption**
- Identify 2-3 staff as "system administrators" (no additional salary—part of existing roles)
- Build maintenance into annual operational budget (~10% of current IT spend, if any)
- Seek integration with government health programs (DOH) that may provide ongoing support

**2. Revenue Diversification**
- Position the system to support donor reporting requirements (donors often fund systems that improve their own accountability)
- Offer anonymized data to public health researchers (with consent)—potential PHP 50,000-100,000/year
- Seek government health IT subsidies (PhilHealth, local government units often fund this)

**3. Open-Source Advantage**
- OpenMRS is free forever—no licensing fees
- No vendor lock-in; can be maintained by any competent IT person
- Large global community means free troubleshooting support

**4. Realistic Risk**
- **If no funding found:** System will degrade in 2-3 years without maintenance
- **Mitigation:** Establish a "Digital Health Fund" (PHP 5,000/month from operations) starting Month 12

---

## Critical Success Factors

| Factor | Action |
|--------|--------|
| **Low digital literacy** | Hire 1 local IT person (PHP 15,000/month) from donor funds—they become permanent staff |
| **Intermittent power** | Solar system is non-negotiable; UPS provides 2-3 hour buffer |
| **Offline capability** | OpenMRS syncs automatically when internet returns; no data loss |
| **Staff turnover** | Create video training in Tagalog; store on tablets for new staff |
| **Paper backup** | Keep parallel paper system for 12 months; don't eliminate until staff confident |

---

## What NOT to Do

❌ Cloud-only systems (Salesforce, Google Workspace) - won't work offline
❌ Proprietary software - creates vendor dependency
❌ Overly complex ERP systems - staff won't use them
❌ Assume "donor will fund Phase 2" - they won't

---

## Bottom Line

**This system is designed to be self-sustaining after 18 months** because:
1. Zero licensing costs (open-source)
2. Hardware is one-time investment
3. Operating costs (~PHP 43,000/year) are modest enough for a 30-person nonprofit to absorb
4. Offline-first design means it degrades gracefully, not catastrophically

**The real risk isn't technology—it's organizational commitment.** If leadership doesn't prioritize the PHP 43,000/year maintenance budget, any system will fail. This approach minimizes that risk by keeping costs low and avoiding vendor lock-in.
